## F01 Loop and built-in tools

- F01.loop-shape — Loop shape [supported, verified] A turn of the agent loop runs from receiving a prompt to producing a response. In the SDKs, read-only tools (like Read, Glob, Grep, and MCP tools marked as read-only) can run concurrently; tools that modify state (like Edit, Write, Bash) run sequentially. query() creates the agentic loop and returns an async iterator used to stream messages. | ev: E-claude-code-00426, E-claude-code-00172, E-claude-code-00752
- F01.turn-limits — Turn and step limits [partial, verified] max_turns (Python) and maxTurns (TypeScript) cap agentic turns (tool-use round trips); a session that reaches its turn limit ends with a result message of subtype error_max_turns. The CLI flag --max-turns limits agentic turns and exits with an error when the limit is reached. | limit: The --max-turns CLI flag is "print mode only" and has "No limit by default"; "A session does not time out on its own" (no top-level session timeout). | ev: E-claude-code-00536, E-claude-code-00399, E-claude-code-07069, E-claude-code-00902

## F02 Context and memory

- F02.context-window-size — Context window size [supported, unverified] Fable models, Sonnet 5 and later, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support a 1 million token context window; see Extended context for availability by plan and how to select a [1m] model. The auto-compact window can be set with CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, or with /autocompact and a token count where the variable isn't set, or per session with --autocompact. | ev: E-claude-code-07422, E-claude-code-06778, E-claude-code-07026
- F02.auto-compaction — Automatic compaction [supported, unverified] Claude Code automatically compacts conversation history when you approach context limits, which preserves important code and decisions while freeing space. In the SDK, it summarizes older history, keeping recent exchanges and key decisions, and emits a system message with subtype compact_boundary. A PreCompact hook fires on a compaction request. | ev: E-claude-code-02218, E-claude-code-00195, E-claude-code-00339
- F02.manual-compaction — Manual compaction [supported, unverified] /compact summarizes the conversation to free space and accepts optional instructions, like /compact Focus on the API changes. - F02.context-inclusion — Context inclusion controls [supported, unverified] The context window accumulates the system prompt, tool definitions, conversation history, tool inputs and tool outputs. - F02.persistent-memory — Persistent memory [supported, verified] Claude can persist learnings across sessions using auto memory: notes Claude writes for itself based on your corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under ~/.claude/projects/. - F02.memory-scope-loading — Memory scope and loading [supported, verified] Auto memory is stored per git repository under ~/.claude/projects/; all worktrees share one directory, and the first 200 lines or 25 KB of the MEMORY.md index load at the start of every session. ## F03 Instruction files

- F03.auto-loaded-files — Auto-loaded files [supported, unverified] CLAUDE.md files load at session start via settingSources, with full content in every request (prompt-cached, so only the first request pays full cost). - F03.import-syntax — Import syntax [supported, verified] CLAUDE.md files import other files with @path/to/import; imported files load into context at launch. Imported files can recursively import others, to a maximum depth of four hops. External imports trigger an approval dialog the first time they are encountered in a project; if declined, they stay disabled. - F03.precedence-scoping — Precedence and scoping [supported, unverified] CLAUDE.md files are additive: all levels contribute to context at once. - F03.path-scoped-rules — Path-scoped rules [supported, verified] Rules are modular instruction files in .claude/rules/ that load alongside CLAUDE.md. - F03.user-vs-project-scope — User and project scope [supported, unverified] Project-scoped configuration lives in a `.claude/` directory at the project root; user-level defaults are at `~/.claude/`. Global preferences apply to every project and load alongside project instructions at the start of every conversation. ## F04 Permission engine

- F04.approval-modes — Approval modes [supported, verified] permission_mode controls how much human oversight you want; the SDK evaluates the active mode with allow and deny rules in a fixed order. Modes named in the docs include acceptEdits, bypassPermissions and dontAsk (which never prompts). set_permission_mode changes the mode for the current session. | ev: E-claude-code-00169, E-claude-code-00406, E-claude-code-00438, E-claude-code-00511
- F04.per-tool-rules — Per-tool rules [supported, unverified] Permission rules allow, ask, or deny specific tools and commands (managed `permissions.allow`, `permissions.deny`). Every tool and bash command can be configured to allow, block, or prompt the user for approval. In the SDK, `allowedTools` auto-approves listed tools without prompting and does not restrict Claude to only those tools. | ev: E-claude-code-00123, E-claude-code-00758, E-claude-code-00954

- F04.trust-prompt — Trust prompt [supported, unverified] If workspace trust hasn't been accepted for a directory, Claude Code shows the workspace trust dialog; accepting saves trust for the workspace. `--bg` checks workspace trust before starting. - F04.bypass-mode — Bypass mode [supported, verified] bypassPermissions runs allowed tools without asking, except those matching an explicit ask rule, connector tools your org set to ask, and tools that require user… A matching deny rule blocks a tool. ## F05 Sandbox and network isolation

- F05.os-sandbox — OS or container sandbox [partial, verified] OS-level filesystem and network isolation is offered through managed sandboxing (`sandbox.enabled`, `sandbox.network.allowedDomains`), and `/sandbox` toggles sandbox mode. Sandboxing restricts shell commands' filesystem and network access. Separately, the SDK can run inside a sandboxed container for process isolation, resource limits, network control, and an ephemeral filesystem. | limit: Sandboxing applies only to Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands and their child processes; `/sandbox` is available on supported platforms only. | ev: E-claude-code-00126, E-claude-code-12218, E-claude-code-00392, E-claude-code-07306
- F05.fs-write-scope — Filesystem write scope [supported, unverified] The sandbox runtime uses OS primitives (`bubblewrap` on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS) to restrict read/write access to configured paths; `allowWrite` lists file path patterns to allow write access to (default empty). Sandboxing restricts filesystem and network access, letting Claude work more freely within defined boundaries. | ev: E-claude-code-00767, E-claude-code-01453, E-claude-code-02202
- F05.network-policy — Network policy [supported, unverified] Managed sandboxing provides OS-level network isolation with domain allowlists (`sandbox.network.allowedDomains`). For production, outbound traffic can be routed through an egress proxy that enforces domain allowlists, injects credentials, and logs requests. `SandboxSettings` lets the SDK configure network restrictions programmatically. | ev: E-claude-code-00126, E-claude-code-00397, E-claude-code-00726
- F05.subprocess-containment — Subprocess containment [partial, verified] Sandboxing's OS-level enforcement applies to Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands and their child processes. | limit: Claude Code runs hooks, MCP servers, and the processes a mod starts outside the sandbox; the mod network policy doesn't cover a program started with `$.process.run`. | ev: E-claude-code-12218, E-claude-code-12582, E-claude-code-12464
- F05.sandbox-override — Sandbox override [supported, unverified] `excludedCommands` entries (for example `docker *`, default empty) bypass sandbox restrictions and run unsandboxed automatically without model involvement. Setting `failIfUnavailable` to `false` falls back to unsandboxed execution with a warning on stderr when the sandbox can't start. Commands typed at the `!` shell-mode prompt run unsandboxed in most sessions. | ev: E-claude-code-00729, E-claude-code-01433, E-claude-code-12847, E-claude-code-11092

## F06 Hooks and lifecycle events

- F06.event-catalog — Event catalog [partial, verified] The SDK provides hooks for different stages of agent execution. Lifecycle events include `PreCompact` (receives a `trigger` field, `manual` or `auto`), `TeammateIdle` (when a teammate is about to go idle), and `DirectoryAdded` (runs after a successful `/add-dir`). | limit: Some hooks are available in both SDKs, while others are TypeScript-only. | ev: E-claude-code-00335, E-claude-code-00199, E-claude-code-01524, E-claude-code-07214
- F06.handler-types — Handler types [supported, unverified] A hook can be a script, HTTP request, MCP tool call, prompt, or subagent triggered by events. A Stop hook can run a script for deterministic checks or a prompt for model-evaluated ones. SDK hooks are callbacks that fire at specific points in the agent loop. | ev: E-claude-code-09250, E-claude-code-09492, E-claude-code-00268
- F06.input-contract — Input contract [supported, unverified] When an event fires and a matcher matches, Claude Code passes JSON context about the event to the hook: for command hooks on stdin, for HTTP hooks as the POST request body. All hook inputs share `session_id`, `cwd`, and `hook_event_name`. Hook input also carries `prompt_id`, a UUID for the current user prompt (requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later). | ev: E-claude-code-09907, E-claude-code-00354, E-claude-code-01230
- F06.output-blocking — Output and blocking semantics [partial, verified] A `PreToolUse` hook runs before the rest of the permission flow and can allow, deny, or modify requests; if it rejects a tool call, the call doesn't execute and Claude receives the rejection message. A `TeammateIdle` hook exits with code 2 to send feedback and keep the teammate working. | limit: A hook that returns `allow` does not skip the deny and ask rules; a `PreToolUse` hook allow also can't approve an `rm` or `rmdir` removal targeting a critical path. | ev: E-claude-code-01463, E-claude-code-00434, E-claude-code-00271, E-claude-code-01524
- F06.matchers — Matcher semantics [supported, verified] The `matcher` field matches a different value depending on the hook event: tool-based hooks match the tool name, while `Notification` hooks match the notification type. Use a single string with `|` to match multiple tools (for example `Edit|Write`); a JSON array means the hook never fires. An empty `matcher` on a Notification hook fires on all notification types. | ev: E-claude-code-00349, E-claude-code-07614, E-claude-code-09711
- F06.config-locations — Configuration locations [supported, unverified] Hooks are configured by editing .claude/settings.json; they are defined under the "hooks" key in settings.json, and there is no standalone hooks file for project or user config. Only plugins load a separate hooks/hooks.json. A customization lockdown can block hooks from user and project sources so they come only from plugins or managed settings. | ev: E-claude-code-07617, E-claude-code-02205, E-claude-code-00130
- F06.trust-enable — Trust and enable controls [partial, verified] An admin can restrict which hooks run and restrict HTTP hook URLs (allowManagedHooksOnly). Hooks in managed settings run shell commands, so interactive users see a security approval dialog before Claude Code applies them. Passing --settings with disableAllHooks set to true turns hooks off for that run. | limit: Without --bare, a -p session runs the hooks in a project's .claude/settings.json, even in a folder you've never trusted, and shows no workspace trust dialog. | ev: E-claude-code-00131, E-claude-code-13381, E-claude-code-12239, E-claude-code-09695

## F07 Managed and enterprise controls

- F07.managed-settings — Managed settings delivery [partial, verified] Endpoint-managed policy loads regardless of setting_sources; resolveSettings() reads MDM sources (macOS plist, Windows HKLM/HKCU). Server-managed settings are fetched when the session authenticates with an organization credential on an eligible ... Claude Tag sessions in a self-hosted environment still read the managed settings file in the runner image. | limit: Claude Tag sessions run in cloud environments but don't receive server-managed settings | ev: E-claude-code-00566, E-claude-code-00940, E-claude-code-00003
- F07.policy-lockdown — Policy lockdown [supported, unverified] Admin setup lists permission rules (permissions.allow, permissions.deny) that allow, ask or deny specific tools and commands. Administrators can enforce disableAgentView, which turns off background agents and agent view, through managed settings. Managed policy settings take precedence over programmatic options. | ev: E-claude-code-00123, E-claude-code-01827, E-claude-code-00597
- F07.model-allowlist — Model allow and deny lists [supported, unverified] availableModels filters which models appear in the picker; adding enforceAvailableModels also constrains the auto-selected default model. It is also enforced server-side at /v1/messages, so a denied model returns 400 regardless of the client; an empty list denies every model. A cloud session rejects a mid-session switch to a model the allowlist excludes. | ev: E-claude-code-00135, E-claude-code-06453, E-claude-code-00001
- F07.identity-sso — Identity and SSO [supported, unverified] Login enforcement restricts login to a specific method or Anthropic organization. Team and Enterprise organizations can require SSO for all users. Developers authenticate with corporate SSO and receive short-lived bearer tokens, so offboarding happens in the IdP. Claude Code has an error for when an organization has disabled API key authentication. | ev: E-claude-code-00132, E-claude-code-07821, E-claude-code-06612, E-claude-code-08304
- F07.data-retention — Data retention and privacy [partial, verified] For Free, Pro and Max accounts, data is used to train new models when the setting is on, including Claude Code use. The default retention period is 30 days and the minimum is 1. Retention of team task lists follows the same cleanupPeriodDays setting you control for session transcripts. Deleting a cloud session permanently removes the session and its data. | limit: The default is 30 days and the minimum is 1; setting 0 fails with a validation error. | ev: E-claude-code-07596, E-claude-code-06843, E-claude-code-01537, E-claude-code-06787
- F07.admin-audit — Admin audit and reporting [supported, verified] Usage monitoring exports OpenTelemetry metrics and lets admins review what the team is running. On Enterprise plans the Compliance API has activity types for GitHub app linking and unlinking. A monitoring event finds machines on an unexpected managed source or that refused to start. ConfigChange fires when an external process or editor modifies a configuration file. | ev: E-claude-code-00143, E-claude-code-07914, E-claude-code-11715, E-claude-code-09729

## F08 Skills

- F08.skill-format — Skill format [supported, verified] A skill is a SKILL.md file in its own folder, such as .claude/skills/name/SKILL.md; a bare .claude/skills/name.md file does not appear in /skills. A skill directory lets you bundle reference docs, templates or scripts alongside the prompt. Hooks can be defined in skill frontmatter in the same configuration format as settings hooks. | ev: E-claude-code-07620, E-claude-code-06816, E-claude-code-10015
- F08.discovery-paths — Discovery paths [supported, unverified] Skills are SKILL.md files in .claude/skills/. Skills also come from plugins and .claude/commands/. A customization lockdown can restrict skills from user and project sources so they come only from plugins or managed settings. /reload-skills re-scans skill and command directories so skills added or changed on disk become available without restarting. | ev: E-claude-code-02206, E-claude-code-08026, E-claude-code-00130, E-claude-code-07295
- F08.invocation — Invocation [supported, verified] Claude gets a list of available skills so it knows what it can invoke; full skill content loads only when Claude uses one. Skills with disable-model-invocation: true are not in that list and stay out of context until you invoke them with /name. One command's entry notes it also activates automatically when your code imports anthropic or @anthropic-ai/sdk. | ev: E-claude-code-07373, E-claude-code-07230
- F08.resource-loading — Resource loading [supported, unverified] Skill descriptions load at session start as short summaries; full content loads only when a skill is invoked. An AgentDefinition skills list preloads the named skills into the agent's context at startup; unlisted skills remain invocable through the Skill tool. | ev: E-claude-code-00194, E-claude-code-10581, E-claude-code-00827
- F08.skill-overrides — Per-skill tool and model overrides [supported, unverified] SKILL.md frontmatter fields include allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model and effort. When a skill is invoked, Claude can use the tools its allowed-tools frontmatter grants. A level that a skill's effort frontmatter set for the flagged request applies to that turn; later turns run at the level the effort resolution order gives the fallback model. | ev: E-claude-code-06839, E-claude-code-09403, E-claude-code-00083

## F09 Subagents and custom agents

- F09.definition-format — Definition format [supported, verified] Subagents are defined in .claude/agents/; each markdown file in agents/ defines a subagent with its own system prompt, tool access, and optionally its own model. A subagent type can come from the project, user, managed, or plugin subagent scope, and a definition can be reused as a delegated subagent and as an agent team teammate. | ev: E-claude-code-02210, E-claude-code-06823, E-claude-code-01541
- F09.tool-allowlist — Tool allow-list [supported, unverified] AgentDefinition's tools field is an array of allowed tool names; if omitted, the agent inherits every tool available to subagents. A teammate from a subagent definition is limited to the definition's tools list. On the CLI, --tools restricts which tools are available. By default a subagent does not get the Agent tool itself, to prevent recursion. | ev: E-claude-code-00600, E-claude-code-01542, E-claude-code-07021, E-claude-code-07387
- F09.per-agent-model — Per-agent model [supported, verified] AgentDefinition.model overrides the model for one agent and accepts an alias such as fable, opus, sonnet, haiku or inherit (inherit uses the main model), or a full model ID. Each markdown file in agents/ can optionally set its own model; for simple subagent tasks the docs suggest model: haiku. When omitted, Claude Code uses the subagent model order. | ev: E-claude-code-00825, E-claude-code-00602, E-claude-code-07490, E-claude-code-06823
- F09.per-agent-effort — Per-agent effort [supported, verified] A subagent's effort field sets its reasoning effort and overrides the session effort level; it defaults to inheriting from the session. Options are low, medium, high, xhigh and max, and AgentDefinition also accepts a number. Available levels depend on the model. Set in subagent markdown frontmatter or on AgentDefinition. | ev: E-claude-code-14746, E-claude-code-00834, E-claude-code-00180, E-claude-code-11518
- F09.nesting-rules — Nesting rules [partial, verified] Subagents can also spawn subagents of their own; the docs link a section on capping nesting depth, concurrency and spend. For messages from a nested subagent, a field gives the agentId of the subagent that spawned it (requires Claude Code v2.1.202 or later). Another page says a subagent gets most of the parent's tools, minus by default the Agent tool itself, to prevent recursion. | limit: Two cited pages differ: E-claude-code-00839 says subagents "can also spawn subagents of their own"; E-claude-code-07387 says a subagent lacks "by default the Agent tool itself to prevent recursion". | ev: E-claude-code-00839, E-claude-code-00935, E-claude-code-07387
- F09.built-in-agents — Built-in agent types [supported, unverified] Built-in subagents include Explore, Plan, and general-purpose. Without a subagent_type, the Agent tool uses the built-in general-purpose subagent, even when you define no agents. The built-in Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md. Setting CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1 disables built-in subagent types and only applies in non-interactive mode (-p). | ev: E-claude-code-09483, E-claude-code-00841, E-claude-code-07623, E-claude-code-07972

## F10 Slash and custom commands

- F10.built-in-commands — Built-in commands [supported, unverified] Built-in commands execute logic coded into the Claude Code process, for example `/compact`. Commands in the set include `/advisor` (set or change the advisor mid-session and save it as your default), `/auto-mode-setup` (drafts `autoMode.environment` entries from your project and recent sessions) and `/bg` (moves an open session into agent view). | ev: E-claude-code-00794, E-claude-code-02132, E-claude-code-00146, E-claude-code-01596
- F10.custom-command-format — Custom command format [supported, verified] Custom commands are flat Markdown files in `.claude/commands/` whose filenames become command names; skills are their recommended successor. A command's frontmatter can name a `model` other than the session's, which makes that turn a model switch. In a plugin, `commands/‹file›.md` becomes `/‹plugin›:‹file›`; a subdirectory adds a segment. | ev: E-claude-code-00797, E-claude-code-12613, E-claude-code-12393
- F10.arguments — Arguments [supported, unverified] A command file can accept parameters with `$ARGUMENTS`, as in `/fix-issue 123`. Built-in commands also take arguments: `/config` accepts `key=value` pairs to set a setting directly, and `/model`, `/effort`, `/fast`, `/color` and `/rename` accept the value as an argument, for example `/model sonnet` (those argument forms require Claude Code v2.1.205 or later). | ev: E-claude-code-06817, E-claude-code-07235, E-claude-code-09660
- F10.discovery-paths — Discovery paths [supported, verified] You can define custom commands as files in `.claude/commands/`, or install them from a plugin; `commands/` is kept for files moved over from `.claude/commands/`. When an added directory and the project both define a command with the same name, Claude Code runs the project's command. `/reload-skills` re-scans skill and command directories without restarting. | ev: E-claude-code-09451, E-claude-code-12392, E-claude-code-12210, E-claude-code-07295
- F10.command-skill-relation — Relation to skills [supported, unverified] A file at `commands/deploy.md` creates `/deploy` the same way a skill at `skills/deploy/SKILL.md` does, and both can be auto-invoked by Claude. Skills use a directory with SKILL.md, letting you bundle supporting files alongside; skills are the recommended way to package multi-step commands. `--disable-slash-commands` disables all skills and commands for a session. | ev: E-claude-code-06815, E-claude-code-09451, E-claude-code-07044

## F11 Plugins and marketplaces

- F11.packaging-format — Packaging format [supported, unverified] A plugin is a directory of components, usually with a manifest: a JSON file at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` giving its name and optionally a version, a description and other metadata. Claude Code loads a plugin without a manifest; inside the file, only `name` is required. A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers as a single installable unit. | ev: E-claude-code-12328, E-claude-code-12371, E-claude-code-09469
- F11.component-types — Component types [partial, verified] Plugins add skills, agents, MCP servers and more; the Claude Security plugin adds one command, `/claude-security`. | limit: Agents shipped in a plugin honor a subset of the subagent fields. | ev: E-claude-code-07657, E-claude-code-06963, E-claude-code-06842
- F11.install-sources — Install sources [supported, unverified] Claude Code registers the official marketplace `claude-plugins-official` the first time a developer starts an interactive terminal session, downloading the catalog from `downloads.claude.ai` and, if that fails, cloning it from `github.com`. The Agent SDK `plugins` option loads custom plugins from local paths. `claude plugin` manages plugins from the CLI. | ev: E-claude-code-06569, E-claude-code-00989, E-claude-code-07000
- F11.versioning-update — Versioning and update [supported, unverified] A plugin manifest can add a version. `/reload-plugins` reloads all active plugins to apply pending changes without restarting. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the plugin's persistent data directory, for dependencies and state that should survive plugin updates. | ev: E-claude-code-12328, E-claude-code-07293, E-claude-code-10011
- F11.trust-signing — Trust and signing [supported, verified] Admins can restrict which marketplace sources users can add and install from. A marketplace's name places it in one of three tiers (official, community, third-party), and Claude Code accepts the official and community names only for marketplaces sourced from `github.com/anthropics/` repositories. Anything a plugin runs, it runs as the user. | ev: E-claude-code-00129, E-claude-code-12585, E-claude-code-12338
- F11.marketplace-hosting — Marketplace hosting [partial, verified] A plugin's marketplace entry is found by walking up from the plugin directory to a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` that lists the plugin. Official and community marketplace names are accepted only for marketplaces sourced from `github.com/anthropics/` repositories. | limit: `extraKnownMarketplaces` applies only after each teammate trusts the folder. | ev: E-claude-code-12368, E-claude-code-14358, E-claude-code-12586

## F12 MCP

- F12.client-support — Client support [supported, unverified] Run `claude mcp add` with a server name and URL or command to connect external tools. MCP tool names start with `mcp__`. SDK sessions that configure MCP servers can also expose MCP prompts as commands. With no SDK elicitation callback, MCP requests for user input that no hook handles are declined automatically. | ev: E-claude-code-02203, E-claude-code-00408, E-claude-code-00802, E-claude-code-00979
- F12.transports — Transports [supported, unverified] MCP servers can use stdio, SSE or HTTP transports. A local stdio server runs as a process Claude Code starts from the `command` and `args` fields of its configuration. An SDK MCP server for custom tools runs in-process inside the application, not as a separate process. `claude mcp login` works for HTTP, SSE and claude.ai connector servers. | ev: E-claude-code-00517, E-claude-code-09463, E-claude-code-00318, E-claude-code-06997
- F12.config-scope — Config location and scope [supported, unverified] Project MCP config goes at the repository root as `.mcp.json`, not inside `.claude/`, with servers under the `mcpServers` key; `.mcp.json` holds project-scoped MCP servers, shared with your team. Admins can deploy a fixed set of servers with `managedMcpServers` or a deployed `managed-mcp.json` file. | ev: E-claude-code-07626, E-claude-code-06788, E-claude-code-00212
- F12.auth — Authentication [supported, verified] `claude mcp login ‹name›` runs a server's OAuth flow without opening the `/mcp` panel, for HTTP, SSE and claude.ai connector servers; `/mcp` also manages OAuth authentication. `MCP_CLIENT_SECRET` supplies the OAuth client secret for servers that need pre-configured credentials. `.mcp.json` takes environment variable references for secrets, such as `${NOTION_TOKEN}`. | ev: E-claude-code-06997, E-claude-code-07273, E-claude-code-08256, E-claude-code-06791
- F12.tool-filtering — Tool filtering and naming [supported, verified] MCP tools are named `mcp__‹server-name›__‹tool-name›`. Deny rules support tool-name globs: `*` matches every tool and `mcp__*` matches every MCP tool across all servers. An agent's `disallowedTools` also accepts `mcp__server` or `mcp__server__*` to remove every tool from that server. By default, MCP tool schemas stay deferred and load on demand via tool search. | ev: E-claude-code-00403, E-claude-code-00453, E-claude-code-00824, E-claude-code-07370
- F12.server-trust — Server trust and approval [partial, verified] Admins can restrict which MCP servers users can add or connect to (allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, managedMcpServers). Project-scoped MCP servers require a one-time approval, visible in /mcp. MCP tools require explicit permission before Claude can use them. | limit: Project trust and MCP server consent dialogs don't relay; those only appear in the local terminal. | ev: E-claude-code-00128, E-claude-code-07628, E-claude-code-00402, E-claude-code-06264

## F13 Sessions, checkpoints, rewind

- F13.resume-continue — Resume and continue [supported, unverified] The SDK continue option continues the most recent conversation. A Python query() call starts fresh unless you pass continue_conversation=True or resume in ClaudeAgentOptions. After /clear, the previous conversation stays on disk and can be reopened by passing its session ID to resume. A resumed subagent retains its full conversation history. | ev: E-claude-code-00957, E-claude-code-00490, E-claude-code-00810, E-claude-code-00860
- F13.fork-branch — Fork or branch a session [supported, verified] With --resume or --continue, --fork-session creates a new session ID instead of reusing the original; the SDK forkSession option does the same when resuming with resume. /branch branches the current conversation to try a different direction, and /fork copies it into a new background session. | ev: E-claude-code-07054, E-claude-code-00966, E-claude-code-07208
- F13.checkpoint-rewind — Checkpoint and rewind [partial, verified] Esc twice or /rewind opens the rewind menu to restore previous conversation and code state, or summarize from a selected message. The SDK enableFileCheckpointing option enables file change tracking for rewinding. Pre-edit file snapshots are kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints. | limit: Checkpointing does not track files modified by Bash commands. | ev: E-claude-code-02216, E-claude-code-00962, E-claude-code-06298, E-claude-code-06847
- F13.transcript-storage — Transcript storage [supported, unverified] Claude Code saves conversations locally. The subprocess writes each batch of transcript entries to local disk first; the SDK then forwards it to your store's append(), so the store mirrors the local transcript. Subagent transcripts are stored in separate files. /export exports the current conversation as plain text. | ev: E-claude-code-02230, E-claude-code-00775, E-claude-code-00866, E-claude-code-07252
- F13.session-listing — Session naming and listing [supported, unverified] /rename renames the current session and shows the name on the prompt bar, or auto-generates a name from conversation history if none is given. claude -r resumes a session by ID or name. The SDK list_sessions() lists past sessions with metadata, filtered by project directory or across all projects. | ev: E-claude-code-07298, E-claude-code-06981, E-claude-code-00499
- F13.cross-surface-handoff — Cross-surface handoff [partial, verified] --teleport and /teleport pull a cloud session into the terminal. --desktop with --continue, or --resume plus a session ID, opens that session in Desktop. In Desktop, choosing Cloud continues the session as a cloud session with the conversation carried over as a summary. | limit: From the CLI, session handoff is one-way: you can pull cloud sessions into your terminal with `--teleport`, but you can't push an existing terminal session to the cloud. | ev: E-claude-code-06736, E-claude-code-07210, E-claude-code-07043, E-claude-code-07758

## F14 Worktrees and parallel execution

- F14.worktree-isolation — Worktree isolation [supported, unverified] Worktrees give each session a separate git checkout, so parallel sessions never edit the same files. Claude creates a git worktree via --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, or subagent isolation: worktree. Each worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch, created from an existing commit, so the repository needs at least one commit first. | ev: E-claude-code-01960, E-claude-code-06793, E-claude-code-07339
- F14.concurrency-caps — Concurrency caps [supported, verified] By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with 'Concurrent subagent limit reached'; a variable sets how many can run before the Agent tool refuses to spawn another (default: 20). In the docs' ultracode section, the limit isn't enforced for Agent-tool subagents. | ev: E-claude-code-14935, E-claude-code-08099, E-claude-code-15834
- F14.parallel-subagents — Parallel subagents [supported, verified] Multiple subagents can run concurrently, so independent subtasks finish in the time of the slowest one. The docs list five ways to work on several tasks at once: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows and projects. The Workflow tool runs a script that orchestrates many subagents in the background. Large parallel-subagent fanouts can hit rate limits. | ev: E-claude-code-00817, E-claude-code-01954, E-claude-code-01274, E-claude-code-00400
- F14.total-agent-caps — Total agent caps [partial, verified] A workflow run is capped at 1,000 agents in total, to prevent runaway loops. There is no limit on the total number of subagents Claude can spawn over a session; the former per-session cap variable was removed in v2.1.224. Once the spend cap is reached, spawning another subagent fails with 'Budget limit reached'. | limit: "There's no limit on the total number of subagents Claude can spawn over a session" (E-claude-code-14937); the cap variable was "Removed in v2.1.224" (E-claude-code-08104). The 1,000-agent total applies per workflow run (E-claude-code-15872). | ev: E-claude-code-15872, E-claude-code-14937, E-claude-code-08104, E-claude-code-00176
- F14.multi-session-coordination — Multi-session coordination [supported, unverified] Claude Code has five ways to work on several tasks at once: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows, and projects. In agent view every prompt starts its own new session, so several can run in parallel. Cross-session messaging lets sessions you run yourself pass findings to each other. | ev: E-claude-code-01954, E-claude-code-01592, E-claude-code-02237

## F15 Background, scheduled and cloud-delegated work

- F15.background-tasks — Background tasks [supported, verified] A session dispatched from agent view keeps running after you close agent view. AgentDefinition.background runs an agent as a non-blocking background task, and stop_task(task_id) stops a running background task. Task messages report background tasks such as backgrounded commands and subagents. | ev: E-claude-code-01587, E-claude-code-00832, E-claude-code-00904, E-claude-code-00518
- F15.scheduled-routines — Scheduled routines [supported, unverified] Claude Code offers three ways to schedule recurring or one-off work. A routine runs a session on a schedule in the cloud, not in parallel on your machine. Desktop scheduled tasks run Claude automatically on a recurring basis. /loop runs a prompt repeatedly while the session stays open; omit the interval and Claude self-paces between iterations. | ev: E-claude-code-07665, E-claude-code-01967, E-claude-code-07660, E-claude-code-07272
- F15.cloud-agents — Cloud agents [supported, verified] Claude Code in the cloud runs sessions on Anthropic-managed infrastructure by default. The --cloud flag starts a cloud session from the command line. Owners can create organization-shared cloud environments that set network access level, environment variables, and a setup script. claude self-hosted-runner hosts cloud sessions on your infrastructure. | ev: E-claude-code-02239, E-claude-code-06737, E-claude-code-00220, E-claude-code-07007
- F15.remote-sessions — Remote sessions [supported, unverified] claude remote-control starts a Remote Control server, with no local interactive session, to control Claude Code from Claude.ai or the Claude app. When a channel declares the permission capability, tool approval prompts are forwarded to it to approve or deny remotely. Projects can run a thread on your computer through Remote Control when you ask. | ev: E-claude-code-07002, E-claude-code-06259, E-claude-code-01957
- F15.event-triggers — Event triggers [supported, unverified] A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into a Claude Code session so Claude can react to things happening outside the terminal. With a prompt input, the Claude Code GitHub Action runs in automation mode on any GitHub event, including a cron schedule. /autofix-pr spawns a cloud session that pushes fixes when CI fails or reviewers leave comments. | ev: E-claude-code-06254, E-claude-code-09400, E-claude-code-07220
- F15.delegation — Delegation to other agents [partial, verified] To involve a different tool, expose it to Claude as an MCP server. An advisor tool lets Claude decide mid-task when to consult a second model. Dispatch is a persistent conversation in the Cowork tab: you message it a task and it decides how to handle it. | limit: In every approach the workers are Claude sessions. | ev: E-claude-code-01959, E-claude-code-07760, E-claude-code-00065

## F16 Surfaces and programmatic control

- F16.interactive-cli — Interactive CLI [supported, unverified] In the terminal, Esc stops Claude mid-action and preserves context so you can redirect. Screen reader mode makes Claude Code write flat text. claude agents opens agent view, one screen to dispatch and monitor sessions running in the background (research preview). | ev: E-claude-code-02215, E-claude-code-00118, E-claude-code-01955
- F16.headless-mode — Headless mode [partial, verified] claude -p runs non-interactively in CI, pre-commit hooks, or scripts; add --output-format stream-json --verbose for streaming JSON output. | limit: In non-interactive mode with `-p`, including Agent SDK sessions, Claude doesn't spawn teammates; with channels in `-p` mode, tools that need terminal input, such as multiple-choice questions and plan mode approval, are disabled. | ev: E-claude-code-02232, E-claude-code-01489, E-claude-code-06297
- F16.ide-integration — IDE integration [supported, unverified] VS Code and JetBrains are listed as Claude Code surfaces that share the same engine as the CLI. From the CLI, /ide manages IDE integrations and shows status, and --ide connects automatically on startup if exactly one valid IDE is available. Claude Code also connects automatically when launched inside a supported IDE's integrated terminal; this can be switched off. | ev: E-claude-code-09484, E-claude-code-07261, E-claude-code-07059, E-claude-code-07997
- F16.desktop-web-app — Desktop and web apps [partial, verified] A Claude Code Desktop app exists: /desktop continues the current session there (alias /app), and the app manages multiple local sessions visually, optionally each in its own worktree. Sessions also appear in the sidebar at claude.ai/code, where you can review changes, share, archive or delete them. | limit: /desktop requires macOS or x64 Windows and a Claude subscription. | ev: E-claude-code-07244, E-claude-code-06764, E-claude-code-02238
- F16.sdk-api — SDK and API [supported, unverified] The SDK is driven through query() calls: every call accepts an options object (Options in TypeScript, ClaudeAgentOptions in Python), a Python query() returns an async iterator that yields messages as they arrive, and the SDK includes the same tools that power Claude Code. allowedTools can pre-approve tools such as Read, Edit and Glob. | ev: E-claude-code-00279, E-claude-code-00161, E-claude-code-00490, E-claude-code-00750
- F16.ci-chat — CI and chat surfaces [partial, verified] A repository setup walks you through selecting a repo and configuring the integration, with an optional step to set up GitHub Actions workflows and secrets. Claude in Slack sessions are automatically shared with Team visibility. claude setup-token generates a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Telegram, Discord, iMessage and fakechat channels are in the research preview. | limit: The repository setup works only with github.com repositories. | ev: E-claude-code-07266, E-claude-code-06784, E-claude-code-07008, E-claude-code-06257

## F17 Model selection and routing

- F17.model-picker — Model picker [supported, verified] The /model picker lets users choose the model; availableModels in managed settings filters which models appear in it, and modelOverrides maps several versions of one family in the /model picker to separate application inference profile ARNs. In agent teams, /model and /fast set the lead's model and fast mode and do not run from a teammate view. | ev: E-claude-code-00135, E-claude-code-02007, E-claude-code-01517, E-claude-code-06464
- F17.model-flag-env — Flag, setting and environment [supported, verified] The model setting sets which model is active when a session starts but is not enforcement: users can pick Default in /model, which resolves to the system's runtime default regardless of what model is set to, unless [quote truncated]. A model option takes a Claude model alias or full model name. fallbackModel is a model to use if the primary fails; it accepts a comma-separated list. | ev: E-claude-code-00015, E-claude-code-00541, E-claude-code-00965
- F17.auto-routing — Automatic routing [supported, verified] When the primary model is overloaded or unavailable, a session with fallbackModel set switches to the backup and retries the primary at the start of each user turn. opusplan applies during plan mode when allowed by availableModels, then switches to Sonnet for execution. Omitted subagent models follow the subagent model order. | ev: E-claude-code-00284, E-claude-code-00159, E-claude-code-00826
- F17.provider-byok — Providers and bring-your-own-key [supported, verified] Claude Code connects to Amazon Bedrock (login wizard under 3rd-party platform), Microsoft Foundry (three authentication methods), Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Claude Platform on AWS and LLM gateways. allowedProviders limits which API providers a machine may use; a session on an unlisted provider is refused (requires v2.1.285 or later). | ev: E-claude-code-01969, E-claude-code-02169, E-claude-code-00417, E-claude-code-00133
- F17.model-catalog — Model catalog and availability [partial, verified] ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{SONNET,OPUS,HAIKU,FABLE}_MODEL control what the sonnet, opus, haiku and fable aliases resolve to. Without the OPUS or SONNET variable, that alias on Amazon Bedrock resolves to Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 4.5. Tools listed under Model availability are available by default only on Claude 3.x models, Opus 4 through 4.7, Sonnet 4 through 4.6 and Haiku 4.5; other models need an opt-in. | limit: Microsoft Foundry "has no startup model check, so requests fail when the default is unavailable" (E-claude-code-02177). | ev: E-claude-code-00016, E-claude-code-01997, E-claude-code-00893, E-claude-code-02177

## F18 Reasoning effort and thinking

- F18.effort-values — Effort values and defaults [supported, verified] The --effort flag accepts low, medium, high, xhigh, max or ultracode, and available levels depend on the model. /effort accepts low to xhigh, max, or auto; CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL accepts low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or auto to use the model default. A new project runs every thread on Opus at high effort by default. | ev: E-claude-code-07046, E-claude-code-07249, E-claude-code-08065, E-claude-code-06898
- F18.where-set — Where effort is set [supported, verified] Effort is set with the --effort flag for the current session and the /effort selector (a slider outside screen reader mode). Writing effortLevel to userSettings saves it as the default effort for the session's current model without changing the running session. The maxEffortLevel managed setting caps effort for every model or per model. | ev: E-claude-code-07046, E-claude-code-00122, E-claude-code-00291, E-claude-code-00137
- F18.model-dependence — Model dependence [supported, verified] Available effort levels depend on the model. Not all models support the effort parameter; effort is supported on Fable models, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 and later. xhigh falls back to high on models that don't support it. | ev: E-claude-code-07047, E-claude-code-09458, E-claude-code-00619, E-claude-code-00177
- F18.thinking-budget-visibility — Thinking budget and visibility [partial, verified] Extended thinking is on by default; thinking tokens bill as output tokens and the default budget can be tens of thousands of tokens per request depending on the model. Thinking is visible step-by-step reasoning, shown in gray italic text in the terminal. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS caps thinking tokens on fixed-budget models; effort levels control adaptive reasoning. | limit: The cap applies 'on models with a fixed thinking budget'; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING 'Has no effect on Fable models, Sonnet 5 and later, or Opus 4.7 and' (quote ends there). | ev: E-claude-code-09459, E-claude-code-08012, E-claude-code-07503, E-claude-code-00095

## F19 Modes and autonomy levels

- F19.named-modes — Named modes [supported, verified] Permission modes are default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk and bypassPermissions; 'manual' is an alias for default, labelled Manual in the UI. By permissiveness: plan, then Manual and dontAsk, then acceptEdits and auto, then bypassPermissions. | ev: E-claude-code-07077, E-claude-code-01762, E-claude-code-07685
- F19.entering-modes — How modes are entered [supported, verified] Shift+Tab cycles permission modes. To enter plan mode, press Shift+Tab until the status bar shows '⏸ plan mode on', or start the session with claude --permission-mode plan. In the SDK, set the mode when calling query() or change it during streaming sessions; Python's set_permission_mode(mode) changes it for the current session. | ev: E-claude-code-02187, E-claude-code-00120, E-claude-code-00466, E-claude-code-00511
- F19.plan-mode — Plan mode [supported, verified] Plan mode explores and plans without editing source files; file edits are never auto-approved and prompt through the canUseTool callback, and file-edit and shell-write tools go there regardless of allow rules. planModeInstructions can replace the default workflow body; the CLI keeps a read-only enforcement preamble and an ExitPlanMode protocol footer. | ev: E-claude-code-00184, E-claude-code-00442, E-claude-code-00988, E-claude-code-02186
- F19.autonomy-mode — Auto-accept and autonomous modes [supported, verified] acceptEdits auto-approves file edits and common filesystem commands (mkdir, touch, mv, cp); other Bash commands follow default rules. Auto mode runs without routine permission prompts by routing tool calls through a classifier that blocks irreversible, destructive or outside-the-environment actions. bypassPermissions skips permission checks, but explicit ask rules still prompt. | ev: E-claude-code-00183, E-claude-code-02097, E-claude-code-00615
- F19.read-only-mode — Read-only or ask mode [partial, verified] Manual mode starts with read-only permissions and asks before editing files, running tests or executing commands; the user approves once or allows from then on. | limit: Not a mode that cannot change files: 'When it needs to edit files, run tests, or execute commands, it asks you first, and you choose whether to approve the action once or allow it from then on.' | ev: E-claude-code-13117
- F19.mode-defaults — Mode defaults and persistence [partial, verified] From Claude Code v2.1.283, auto mode is the built-in starting permission mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions. A setting lets you choose the starting mode for your developers' terminal sessions instead of the built-in one, or remove auto mode. In Desktop, a picked mode is remembered per folder and takes precedence over defaultMode for that folder. | limit: Desktop picks are remembered per folder 'except Plan, which applies to the current session only'; a first session after install or upgrade 'can also start in a different permission mode than your later sessions do'. | ev: E-claude-code-02197, E-claude-code-00125, E-claude-code-07686, E-claude-code-08288

## F20 Version, release channel, update path

- F20.version-at-retrieval — Version at retrieval [supported, verified] The changelog has an entry labelled 2.1.289, dated October 3, 2026. | ev: E-claude-code-17023
- F20.release-channels — Release channels [supported, unverified] Claude Code has a stable and a latest release channel. The autoUpdatesChannel setting controls which one it follows for auto-updates and claude update, and claude install accepts a version number or the stable or latest channel names. The Homebrew claude-code cask tracks stable (typically about a week behind, skipping releases with major regressions). | ev: E-claude-code-19820, E-claude-code-13588, E-claude-code-14386, E-claude-code-06983
- F20.update-mechanism — Update mechanism [supported, verified] Claude Code auto-updates and can also be updated with claude update: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER stops only background updates while claude update still works, and DISABLE_UPDATES is for when laptops must not fetch releases. minimumVersion prevents auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum. Version checks and downloads go directly to Anthropic, separate from the gateway path. | ev: E-claude-code-06567, E-claude-code-00138, E-claude-code-09325
- F20.changelog-source — Changelog source [supported, unverified] /release-notes shows the changelog in an interactive version picker, with the notes appearing in your transcript without entering the conversation Claude sees. A cached copy is kept at cache/changelog.md and refreshed in the background. The changelog page lists dated Update entries labelled by version, for example 2.1.286 on September 30, 2026. | ev: E-claude-code-07292, E-claude-code-06874, E-claude-code-02441
- F20.deprecation-policy — Deprecation policy [supported, unverified] Removals and renames are marked in the flag and command references: --enable-auto-mode is marked Removed in v2.1.111 (use --permission-mode auto), /pr-comments Removed in v2.1.91 (ask Claude directly), and --remote still works as a deprecated alias for --cloud. On the gateway page, breaking changes to the protocol are announced in advance, but indefinite backwards compatibility isn't guaranteed. | ev: E-claude-code-07049, E-claude-code-07287, E-claude-code-06739, E-claude-code-06627

## F21 Relationship to host platform

- F21.host-platform — Host platform [partial, verified] Host platforms can embed Claude Code and manage model provider routing on its behalf, signalled by CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST. Cowork in the Claude Desktop app runs its sessions on Claude Code. | limit: When a host platform sets the variable, 'Claude Code ignores provider-selection, endpoint, and authentication variables'; in a Cowork session Claude Code 'never fetches server-managed settings from the claude.ai admin console'. | ev: E-claude-code-08143, E-claude-code-10965
- F21.shared-account-billing — Shared account and billing [partial, verified] Plan usage is shared across all Claude Code surfaces (Desktop's usage ring shows context window and plan usage), and project usage counts against the same plan limits as other Claude Code sessions. The supervisor and its sessions authenticate with the same stored credentials as interactive sessions. | limit: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: 'When set, this key is used instead of your Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription even if you are logged in.' | ev: E-claude-code-07730, E-claude-code-06940, E-claude-code-07928, E-claude-code-01818
- F21.shared-execution-infrastructure — Shared execution infrastructure [supported, verified] Cloud sessions run on an Anthropic-managed cloud VM by default; local sessions process code on the user's own machine. Sessions an organization routes to a self-hosted environment run on infrastructure the organization operates. | ev: E-claude-code-15404, E-claude-code-18037, E-claude-code-18261, E-claude-code-22141
- F21.shared-model-selection — Shared model selection [supported, verified] Claude Code runs on the same models as the Claude app. Desktop and the CLI make the same models available; in Desktop the model is selected from the dropdown next to the send button and can be changed mid-session from the same dropdown. | ev: E-claude-code-07887, E-claude-code-07345
- F21.shared-agent-runtime — Shared agent runtime [supported, verified] All surfaces (CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Desktop, claude.ai) share the same engine; Claude Code behaves the same everywhere, and what changes is where the session runs and whether local configuration is available. The Agent SDK embeds Claude Code's autonomous agent loop and is built on the same foundation. | ev: E-claude-code-09484, E-claude-code-15403, E-claude-code-16054, E-claude-code-16072
- F21.delegates-to — Delegates to [partial, verified] In a self-hosted environment, a cloud session's clone and everything after it run on the organization's own runners, where network boundaries, setup and push behavior are operator-configured. | limit: The quote covers hand-off to the organization's own runners, not a named sibling surface: 'The steps below describe Anthropic-hosted sessions. In a self-hosted environment, the clone and everything after it run on your organization's own runners'. | ev: E-claude-code-23049
- F21.distinct-harness-features — Distinct harness features [supported, verified] Some plugin components are Claude Code-only and don't load on claude.ai or in Cowork; a component support table lists each by app. Claude apps gateway is Anthropic's own gateway, built into the claude binary and tested alongside each Claude Code release. | ev: E-claude-code-21229, E-claude-code-20219, E-claude-code-06611

## F22 Usage, cost, limits and observability

- F22.usage-visibility — Usage and cost visibility [supported, verified] /usage shows session totals, and a session cost summary is printed when Claude Code exits if the account shows costs. Every SDK result subtype carries total_cost_usd, usage, num_turns and session_id. /context shows context window usage by category, skill and tool, and an SDK method returns the same breakdown. | ev: E-claude-code-00158, E-claude-code-00206, E-claude-code-00262, E-claude-code-01038
- F22.budget-caps — Budgets and caps [partial, verified] --max-budget-usd caps API spend before stopping, and spend from subagents counts toward the cap. The SDK max_budget_usd and maxBudgetUsd options stop the query when the client-side cost estimate reaches a USD value, and options can also limit turns, cost and reasoning depth. | limit: --max-budget-usd is print mode only. The SDK option counts only the call's own spend; totals restored from a resumed session don't count. | ev: E-claude-code-07067, E-claude-code-00537, E-claude-code-00975, E-claude-code-00174
- F22.rate-limits — Rate-limit behaviour [supported, unverified] When a claude.ai usage limit blocks a request, /rate-limit-options shows ways to keep working, including waiting to continue automatically when the limit resets and adding usage credits. Project usage counts against the same plan limits as other sessions. If the usage request fails, /usage shows the last usage bars it loaded within the past 60 minutes. | ev: E-claude-code-07290, E-claude-code-06940, E-claude-code-07441
- F22.telemetry-otel — Telemetry and OpenTelemetry [supported, unverified] OpenTelemetry export sends metrics from each developer's machine to your own observability stack, with per-user token counts, costs and tool activity. With CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 set, each step of the agent loop becomes a trace span. The prompt_id field matches the prompt.id attribute on OpenTelemetry events. | ev: E-claude-code-07469, E-claude-code-00425, E-claude-code-01230
- F22.logs-debug — Logs and debug output [supported, unverified] Per-session debug logs are written to debug/ while debug logging is on, started with --debug or /debug; the log is at ~/.claude/debug/‹session-id›.txt. claude logs ‹id› prints the session's recent output. The SDK debug option enables debug mode for the Claude Code process. | ev: E-claude-code-06849, E-claude-code-06308, E-claude-code-01782, E-claude-code-00958
- F22.status-display — Status line and display [supported, verified] The statusLine setting customizes the line shown at the bottom while Claude works, and a custom status line can track context usage continuously. /status shows an API provider line (for example Microsoft Foundry with the resource name or base URL you configured) and, in auto mode, an Auto mode server row reading Enabled or Disabled. | ev: E-claude-code-02185, E-claude-code-06802, E-claude-code-02183, E-claude-code-02095
